item.title: Formal Verification of Lane-Changing Algorithms
item.description:
Institution

System Analysis and Verification (SAVe) Lab, SEECS, NUST
Jan 2024 - Jan 2025

Project Description

Lane changing is one of the most complex things an autonomous vehicle does, and it is usually checked in simulation, which can miss rare corner cases. For my MS thesis I analyzed lane-changing algorithms formally instead, so the results hold for every behavior the model allows, not just the runs we happened to simulate.

Project Highlights

  • Modeled the MOBIL lane-changing algorithm together with the Intelligent Driver Model as a Markov Decision Process.
  • Wrote safety, lane-change efficiency, timing and robustness requirements in PCTL and checked them with the PRISM probabilistic model checker.
  • Built the model from generic parts, so other lane-changing algorithms can be plugged into the same framework.
  • The work was published in the Journal of Signal Processing Systems in 2026.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Probabilistic Model Checking
  • PRISM
  • Markov Decision Processes
  • PCTL

item.title: LLM-Guided Heuristics for SAT Solvers
item.description:
Institution

System Analysis and Verification (SAVe) Lab, SEECS, NUST
Jun 2025 - Present

Project Description

SAT solvers depend on carefully tuned heuristics. In this project I look at whether large language models can help design them, without fine-tuning the model itself. A lot of recent work lets the model reflect on its earlier attempts, so we also asked a simple question: does that reflection actually help?

Project Highlights

  • Developing neuro-symbolic frameworks that combine LLMs with SAT solver heuristics.
  • Ran a placebo-controlled study to test whether LLM reflection really improves the heuristics it produces.
  • Evolved phase-initialisation heuristics for CaDiCaL. The best ones ran 48% faster on the DFVS benchmarks and 37% faster on the decision-tree benchmarks than the best default setup.
  • The manuscript is complete, with Osman Hasan and S. Abed.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • SAT Solving
  • CaDiCaL
  • Large Language Models
  • Experimental Design

item.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection in Encrypted Video Traffic
item.description:
Institution

Data Science & Machine Learning Lab, SINES, NUST
Feb 2025 - May 2025

Project Description

Video traffic is encrypted, so a classifier only sees patterns in the packets, not the content. It also needs to notice when traffic does not look like anything it was trained on, instead of confidently guessing. I led the lab’s project on this out-of-distribution (OOD) detection problem for encrypted YouTube traffic.

Project Highlights

  • Designed the data pipelines and the deep learning models.
  • Wrote the first draft of the paper, “Unified Framework for YouTube Traffic Classification and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Encrypted Networks”, which the lab plans to resubmit.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Deep Learning
  • Out-of-Distribution Detection
  • Network Traffic Analysis

item.title: Interactive Formal Verification Lab
item.description:
I built these three tools to show how some of the ideas I work with actually behave. They are small, but they are real: the model checker explores every reachable state and checks your formula with the standard labelling algorithm, and the verifier computes weakest preconditions for whatever conditions you type in. Everything runs in your browser, so feel free to break things.

Solver Controls

Join clauses with & and literals with |. Negate with ~ or !. Up to 12 variables.

Assignment

Solver log

Clauses and search tree IDLE

Clauses

Search tree

Decision Forced by unit propagation Conflict or dead end Satisfying path

Model Checking

Formula syntax

Atoms compare a variable with a value, like pc0 = WAIT or turn != 1. Booleans can stand alone, like flag0 or deadlock.

Connectives: ! & | -> <->. Temporal operators: AX EX AF EF AG EG, plus A[p U q] and E[p U q].

Current state: S0

Model checker log

Reachable states IDLE

Hover a state or an arrow for details. Click a state one step away from the current one to move there.

Initial state Satisfies the formula Current state Counterexample Witness Deadlock

Program Verification

Weakest precondition trace

Annotated program and verification conditions IDLE

Program

Verification conditions

VCs are checked by trying every integer combination in a small range, so a pass is strong evidence rather than a proof. Only partial correctness is checked here, not termination.

What you are looking at

DPLL SAT solver. A SAT solver decides whether a propositional formula has a satisfying assignment. DPLL guesses a value for one variable, follows every consequence it is forced into (unit propagation), and backtracks when a clause becomes false. The tree shows guesses as circles and forced assignments as diamonds. The pigeonhole example is worth stepping through: you cannot put three pigeons into two holes without two of them sharing, and the solver has to rule out every option before it can say so.

CTL model checker. The four systems are written as small guarded-command programs. The checker builds every reachable state from them, then works out which states satisfy each part of your formula, from the inside out. Press Step to watch that happen one subformula at a time. When a property fails you get a counterexample run, and for properties like EF you get a witness. Peterson’s algorithm passes everything. Remove the turn variable and it still keeps the processes apart, but it can deadlock. The naive lock fails at the most basic job, and the checker shows you the exact interleaving that breaks it.

Hoare logic verifier. A Hoare triple {P} S {Q} says that if P holds before program S runs, then Q holds after it. The verifier works backwards from Q, computing the weakest precondition of each statement, and turns the result into verification conditions (VCs). Loops need an invariant, which you provide. You can edit any of the conditions. Try weakening an invariant and see which VC breaks, and what counterexample it gives you.

Why this matters

Testing can show that a program works on the inputs you tried. Formal verification aims to show that it works on all of them, or to find the case where it does not. That is why these ideas show up wherever failures are expensive: hardware design, operating system kernels like seL4, flight software and communication protocols. Real tools are far more capable than these toys, but the core ideas are the same.

Text Categorization Using Encoder only Transformer
item.description:
Institution

National University of Sciences and Technology, Islamabad, Pakistan
Dec 2023 - Jan 2024

Project Description

The goal here was to sort text into a fixed set of categories automatically. I used an encoder-only transformer, the same family as BERT, because it builds a representation of the whole input, which suits classification well.

Project Highlights

  • Built a text categorization model on an encoder-only transformer architecture.
  • Evaluated and fine-tuned the model so it categorized a varied mix of text reliably.
  • Implemented everything in Python with Hugging Face Transformers and scikit-learn.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Python
  • Natural Language Processing (NLP)
  • Transformers
  • Text Classification
  • Machine Learning

item.title: Sentiment Analysis Using BERT
item.description:
Institution

National University of Sciences and Technology, Islamabad, Pakistan
Oct 2023 - Dec 2023

Project Description

For this project I built a sentiment classifier using BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers). BERT reads each word in the context of the whole sentence, which matters a lot for sentiment, where a single word like “not” can flip the meaning.

Project Highlights

  • Fine-tuned pre-trained BERT models for sentiment classification instead of training from scratch.
  • Prepared the text data with standard NLP preprocessing before training.
  • Wrote the pipeline in Python using HuggingFace Transformers and TensorFlow.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Python
  • Natural Language Processing (NLP)
  • BERT
  • Machine Learning
  • Data Preprocessing

item.title: Multiclass Image Classification using Transfer Learning
item.description:
Project Description

I built a multiclass image classifier on top of InceptionResNetV2. Rather than training a large network from scratch, I started from a pre-trained model and reused what it had already learned, then trained it to recognize my own set of classes.

Project Highlights

  • Used InceptionResNetV2 as the base model and adapted it to the target classes through transfer learning.
  • Added data augmentation and input normalization so the model would do better on images it had not seen during training.
  • Wrote the full training and evaluation pipeline in Python.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Python
  • Deep Learning
  • Transfer Learning
  • Computer Vision
  • Data Augmentation

item.title: Adaptive Irrigated Agriculture Monitoring (Embedded + Cloud)
item.description:
Project Description

This was an IoT system for keeping track of conditions in the field. Embedded sensor nodes measured soil and air conditions and sent the readings to the cloud in real time, so irrigation could follow what the crop actually needed instead of a fixed schedule.

Project Highlights

  • Built the embedded sensor setup that reads soil and air conditions.
  • Connected the sensor nodes to the cloud for real-time monitoring.
  • Used the incoming data to decide when and how much to irrigate.

Technical Skills Acquired

  • Embedded Systems
  • IoT
  • Sensors
  • Cloud Integration
